label: Does the burst depend on AMPA-receptor drive?
observed: In the neuron-specific knockout slice an NMDA-receptor antagonist abolishes the spontaneous bursts. No AMPA/kainate antagonist has been applied; a shift of the knockout excitatory-current amplitude fits an AMPA-type quantum only by inference.
hypothesised: The burst may also need AMPA-receptor drive. This is exploratory; the premise is not established.
alternatives: NMDA-receptor-regenerative drive (GluN2B- or GluN2A-weighted), a general loss of excitatory drive, and a recording-state artefact. Kainate receptors are not separated from AMPA receptors by the usual tools.
strengthen: A verified AMPA/kainate block that abolishes the bursts at less total charge removed than the NMDA-receptor antagonist needs would put AMPA receptors first in the next question.
weaken: Bursts that persist under a verified, pre-specified AMPA/kainate block weaken this reading. Abolition alone does not separate AMPA drive from NMDA-receptor-regenerative drive, because losing the depolarisation also removes magnesium relief.
source_rows: ampa_nmda hypotheses.tsv BH1; prediction_matrix M07, M08

label: Is the NMDA-receptor dependence total receptor gain or GluN2B-weighted?
observed: The burst needs NMDA-receptor activity; about 20 percent of the delayed evoked response remains against the wild-type floor under the antagonist, which is not evidence of incomplete block.
hypothesised: A GluN2B-selective negative modulator may remove the bursts at a smaller measured fraction of the isolated NMDA-receptor current than the full antagonist needs. Exploratory.
alternatives: Total NMDA-receptor reduction, a GluN2A-weighted component, a general loss of drive, and a bath-state (magnesium, potassium) effect.
strengthen: A curve shifted to the left of the full-antagonist curve, with a measured sensitive fraction, makes the GluN2B-directed comparison the better question.
weaken: Coincident curves make total NMDA-receptor reduction (with the bath magnesium and voltage) the question; a plateau below abolition moves it to GluN2A-containing receptors. None of this can come from other preparations.
source_rows: ampa_nmda hypotheses.tsv BH2; prediction_matrix M04, M05, M06

label: Can the gap-junction tool's burst fall be read as a gap-junction result?
observed: A gap-junction-blocking tool lowered the burst rate in the knockout slice and did not recover. In culture the same tool lowers AMPA and NMDA currents, broadens spikes and lowers input resistance.
hypothesised: The fall may come from effects on synaptic currents and excitability rather than from coupling. No datum in the sources read supports the gap-junction half. Exploratory.
alternatives: Reduced release or altered excitability; direct NMDA-receptor channel block (neither shown nor excluded); neuronal electrical coupling; pannexin-1; run-down or a recording artefact.
strengthen: A residual fall beyond a control matched to the same measured current reduction, together with a loss of coupling, keeps the connexin question open.
weaken: If a matched non-gap-junction control gives the same fall, the gap-junction attribution is not supported; a pannexin-1 blocker with shown engagement that lowers bursts would support pannexin-1.
source_rows: ampa_nmda hypotheses.tsv BH3; prediction_matrix M09, M10, M11

label: Do passive cell size and a resting K+ conductance explain the larger sag and input resistance?
observed: Input resistance rises 39 percent in mutants while the time constant is nearly unchanged; resting potential and sag grade with gene dose. Recordings use one fixed current step.
hypothesised: Under a single-compartment assumption the numbers do not fit a pure loss of resting K+ conductance at constant capacitance; smaller cells plus a conductance change is one reading. Capacitance is not an established difference. No drug is proposed.
alternatives: Smaller cells with a fixed seal leak, a larger Ih, selection by input-resistance criteria, maturation delay, and a cell-type mix.
strengthen: Capacitance and time constant measured in the same cells, or a Ba2+- or Kv7-blocker-sensitive difference current in Wwox neurons, would decide whether any pharmacological arm is needed.
weaken: If sag remains at matched potential and deflection, or capacitance is unchanged while input resistance is higher, the passive reading fails.
source_rows: membrane hypotheses.tsv MH1; experiments E1, E3

label: Does an Ih (HCN) contribution remain after matching potential and deflection?
observed: Sag and rebound are larger in the knockout; no Ih-blocker arm and no voltage-clamp current exist in the records read. In normal cortex an Ih blocker reduces sag.
hypothesised: An HCN contribution may remain after matching conditions. This is a tool arm only: two blocker chemotypes, engagement first. No candidate drug and no in-vivo claim.
alternatives: The passive and leak reading (MH1), a T-type contribution to rebound, off-target sodium-current block of the tool, another HCN isoform or compartment.
strengthen: A matched-condition excess sag blocked by both chemotypes with a larger voltage-clamp Ih density would move HCN from 'contributes' to 'differs'.
weaken: If the excess vanishes at matched conditions, or the blocker-sensitive current per pF is the same, there is no HCN difference. A blocker response shows contribution, not a defect.
source_rows: membrane hypotheses.tsv MH2; experiments E1, E2

label: Were the intrinsic recordings made under conditions that bias the genotype contrast?
observed: The Methods drug list contains no synaptic blocker, so the intrinsic recordings were probably made with synapses intact, while most knockout slices burst.
hypothesised: Part of the contrast may reflect network state or cell selection rather than a cell-autonomous difference. This is a design control; no drug is proposed.
alternatives: A genuine cell-autonomous difference (MH1 or MH2), maturation delay, a cell-type mix.
strengthen: An explicit statement of the recording conditions, or recordings under blockade with identity by morphology and matched access resistance.
weaken: If the contrast is unchanged under blockade with matched access resistance, it is intrinsic to the recorded membrane; if it shrinks, the original contrast was partly synaptic state or selection.

label: A TREK-1 (and TASK-1) pool closed by a lower interstitial pH is part of the Wwox Rin and rest pair
observed: Rin +39 percent, rest +5.6 mV, implied E_K-like reversal (SCI43); adult TREK1-/- doubles Rin in S1 layers 2-4; TASK-1/3 double knock-out removes 26 percent of the holding current in P9-15 layer V
hypothesised: extracellular acid closes both channels (recombinant pH50 7.3-7.5); closure removes a K+ conductance (INFERENZA). Exploratory: the package states no therapeutic direction.
alternatives: KP2: A TASK-3 closure by acid explains the pair (the coda's DREAM chain) || KP3: A lactate-driven intracellular acidification acts on these channels in the recorded cell || KP4: A tool-by-pH interaction is the discriminating action: an occlusion test of the closed share || KP5: Metabolic change without relevant acidification acts through a K+ conductance not set by pH (KATP, or a direct lactate action on TREK1)
strengthen: If E1 holds: the genotype difference in Rin shrinks at acid pHo (occlusion) and the pH-sensitive current per pF is larger in wild type
